small_guidance:
- Add larger tiles to the autotune list now that small variants compile: `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16` at `num_warps=8, num_stages=2` and `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32` at `num_stages=3`. With OH*OW=15876 and OC=128 the GEMM is M-heavy; bigger BLOCK_M reduces weight re-loads.
- Hoist the `(ic, kh, kw)` decomposition out of the K-loop by precomputing arrays of length `K` only once, or better: split the K-loop into a nested `ic` outer × `KH*KW=9` inner pair so `kh*stride_xh + kw*stride_xw` becomes compile-time constants and weight indexing collapses to contiguous loads.
- Swap program-id ordering so `pid_m` (spatial) is axis-0 and `pid_n` (OC) is axis-1, with N as axis-2, and add an L2-friendly swizzle (group along OC) to improve weight reuse across batch.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM with NHWC (channels-last) input/output layout so the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW) is contiguous in memory; this lets `tl.load` issue 128-bit coalesced loads per row instead of strided gathers across IC. Reorder weight to `(KH, KW, IC, OC)` for the same reason on the W side.
- Make the kernel persistent and unroll the 3×3 spatial kernel explicitly (KH=KW=3 are compile-time constants in this model): loop only over IC with `BLOCK_K` tiling along IC, and inside the loop do 9 separate `tl.dot` accumulations with statically-offset input pointers. This eliminates the integer divmod in the K-loop entirely.
- Fuse the bias add + ReLU + second bias add into the epilogue (already done) but also fuse the N-batch dimension into the M tile (M = N*OH*OW) so one program covers multiple batch elements with the same weight tile, dramatically increasing weight reuse — the current per-batch launch reloads the OC×K weight slab N=128 times.
